title: Dyson Just Dropped New Lidar-Guided Robot Vacuums. Which One’s Worth It?
gist: Dyson launched three robot vacuums in a new Nurovi line — the R1 Dry at $550, the R2 Wash+Dry at $700 sold exclusively through Costco, and the R3 Spot+Scrub UV at $1,200 — switching navigation from HD camera to lidar and adding a Twin-Capture dust system, with the top model using UV light to find floor stains. The write-up is a pre-review overview; the author flags the R2's price-to-spec ratio as the most intriguing and is skeptical that maximum suction correlates with best results.

insights.claim: Dyson launched three robot vacuums in a new line at $550 for the vacuum-only R1, $700 for the R2 vacuum-mop hybrid, and $1,200 for the top-of-the-line R3 with UV stain detection.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A premium brand now spans a $550 to $1,200 ladder in robot vacuums, pushing down into mid-market price bands.
insights.quote: the Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry ($550), the Dyson R2 Nurovi Wash + Dry ($700), and the Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV ($1,200)

insights.claim: The mid-tier R2 will only be available at Costco while the R1 and R3 will be sold on the manufacturer's own website and presumably other retailers.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A club-channel exclusive on the best price-to-spec model is a deliberate volume bet that gates the most attractive SKU behind a membership.
insights.quote: The only downside is that you need a Costco membership to purchase one, as it's a Costco exclusive.

insights.claim: The launch is part of a broader September product wave from the company that also included vacuums and an electric toothbrush with a built-in camera.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Dense fall product cycles compress reviewer attention and make comparative testing lag launches.

insights.claim: All three models feature lidar laser-precision navigation, whereas the company's previous robot vacuum relied on an HD camera.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Abandoning camera navigation for lidar aligns the brand with the category standard and sidesteps in-home camera privacy objections.
insights.quote: They also feature lidar laser-precision navigation—Dyson's last robot vacuum relied on an HD camera

insights.claim: All three share a Twin-Capture System designed to pick up dust and debris on both hard floors and carpets, while the base stations retain canister-style compartments that keep the brand's distinctive look.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Shared core mechanics across the price ladder mean differentiation comes from mopping and stain detection, not suction hardware.

insights.claim: The R2 promises 21,000 Pa of suction and uses triangle-style mopping pads, a design the reviewer calls unique and hopes will handle corners well.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Corner coverage is a persistent weak point in robot mopping, so pad geometry is a genuine differentiator to test.
insights.quote: It promises 21,000 Pa of suction, which is a nice amount of power.

insights.claim: The flagship R3 packs 30,000 Pa of suction and incorporates AI that the manufacturer says can identify up to 200 types of household substances and clean them until they're gone.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Substance-classification AI is becoming the premium differentiator in home robotics, shifting the pitch from suction to recognition.
insights.quote: Dyson says can identify up to 200 types of household substances and clean them until they're gone

insights.claim: The highest suction figure does not always produce the best cleaning results in the reviewer's experience.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Pascal ratings are a marketing axis more than a performance guarantee, which undercuts spec-led purchase decisions.
insights.quote: though I don't always find the highest suction makes for the best results

insights.claim: The reviewer was not impressed by the predecessor Spot+Scrub Ai model because it did not really seem to find stains, making the new UV-based stain detection the key open question for the flagship.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A prior generation failing at its headline feature is the strongest reason to discount the new model's marketing claims until tested.
insights.quote: I wasn't super impressed by the previous Spot+Scrub Ai, since it didn't really seem to find stains.

insights.claim: The entry-level R1 is a vacuum-only option best suited to mostly carpet and soft flooring, but comparably priced competitors offer both vacuuming and mopping.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A vacuum-only device at $550 faces direct pressure from hybrid rivals at the same price, questioning its positioning.
insights.quote: you can find other vacuums for this price that do both

insights.claim: The mid-tier R2 is the most intriguing of the three because it lands at nearly half the price of the flagship while retaining lidar navigation and the new dust-capture technology.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Value concentrates in the middle SKU, which is precisely the one locked behind a warehouse-club membership.
insights.quote: This is the vacuum I'm most intrigued about. It's a great price point—nearly half the price of the Spot+Scrub model

insights.claim: None of the three models had been tested at the time of writing, with a full comparative review promised after testing.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: All performance claims in the piece are vendor-supplied, so the assessment carries no independent verification yet.
insights.quote: I'll be testing these soon to see how they measure up against similar vacuums
